system_note: Reviewed Cascade Health PPO Readmission Review Guideline and the index (MR_01) documentation. Cascade's guideline applies a 30-day review window ("30 days from prior discharge") and asks whether the readmission diagnosis is the same as, or clinically related to, the condition treated during the prior stay (B1). The readmission falls within the payer's review window (gap_days = 21). The readmission principal diagnosis is J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) and that exact code was also billed on the index stay. Index narrative documents ongoing ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy and active plans for trach-collar weaning at discharge (Admit: 2026-01-06 Transfer: 2026-04-11; Discharge diagnoses include "ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy (weaning)"). Per Cascade policy B1, a readmission where the readmission diagnosis is the same as or clinically related to the prior stay qualifies as a Finding. Section C exclusions were reviewed (direct transfers, scheduled readmissions, LTAC/SNF/IRF admissions, etc.); none of those exclusions are documented in the retrieved records for this readmission. Evidence used: Cascade guideline review-window and B1 criterion (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Cascade Health PPO - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, positions 4 and 12), the get_index_claim linkage note showing the readmission principal diagnosis is also billed on the index stay (get_index_claim result for MR_01), and the index Discharge / Transfer Summary documenting persistent ventilator-dependent respiratory failure and the 04/11/2026 transfer. Therefore, the readmission is a Finding under the payer's "same or related condition" criterion (readmission related to the index respiratory failure).
rationale_letter: Re: Readmission review for RM_01 (prior admission MR_01) We completed a readmission review per Cascade Health PPO's Readmission Review Guideline (effective 03/01/2024). Cascade's guideline applies a 30-day review window from the prior discharge. The readmission for RM_01 occurred 21 days after discharge from MR_01 and is therefore within the 30-day review window. Finding: This readmission is related to the index admission and qualifies as a Finding under the guideline's "same or related condition" criterion. Basis: The readmission principal diagnosis is J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia), which is also billed on the index stay (MR_01). The index discharge summary documents ongoing ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy and active weaning plans at the time of transfer on 04/11/2026. Cascade's guideline (Section B1) explicitly states that when the readmission diagnosis is the same as, or clinically related to, the condition treated during the prior stay, the readmission qualifies as a Finding. No exclusions (for example, a documented direct transfer or scheduled readmission) were identified in the records retrieved for this review. Correction: Based on this Finding, the readmission RM_01 is determined to be clinically related to the prior index stay MR_01 under Cascade Health PPO policy and will be processed per the payer's readmission adjustment rules. If you disagree with this determination, please submit any additional supporting clinical documentation (for example, the readmission admission note or other contemporaneous records demonstrating an unrelated new acute event) for reconsideration. Sincerely, Clinical Readmission Auditor
